name: Bladee
discourse_profile: Bladee treats music-making as world-building — visual before sonic, spiritual before technical. He describes wanting to 'make a picture' rather than a song, and cites painter Hilma af Klint's autonomous symbolic systems as a primary inspiration: 'She made systems of all this stuff, which was really inspiring to me.' His lyrics have moved toward radical minimalism — 'The more I do it, the more I want to say basically nothing. It's more like a pure reflection' — pursuing economy of language as a form of universality rather than obscurity. He rejects genre as a frame ('Genre is limiting yourself. Just be yourself and let that be the genre'), positioning Drain Gang's output as a self-contained universe with its own logic rather than a contribution to any existing tradition. The concept of 'drain' itself operates as a metaphysics of exchange — loss and gain, emotional catharsis, extraction of essence. Post-2020, his work is explicitly rooted in spirituality — his own syncretic system drawn from Buddhism, Christianity, and personal cosmology — with the persona 'Bladee' functioning as 'me on a higher dimension.' The creative process is improvised: lyrics written in-studio, top-of-mind, bar by bar, with songs built in single sessions around mantric repetition.
